subject: Clarifying: training exclusions and retention / deletion timeline for OliveHealth
messages:
From: Rajiv Shah <rajiv.shah@olivehealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarifying training guarantees + retention windows

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. OliveHealth's InfoSec team has two quick follow-ups before we bring this to procurement: 1) your statement in the deck that Redwood 'does not train models on customer data' — can you confirm the exact scope of that? Does it apply to hosted API requests, Dedicated, and Private (VPC) deployments equally? 2) We need a clear deletion/retention timeline that covers: request acknowledgement, deletion from primary storage, removal from backups, and any logs/analytics where message-level content could remain.

Can you send a short FAQ we can include in the assessment? If you have SOC2 artifacts that reference retention controls, please attach.

Regards,
Rajiv
Director, IT Security
OliveHealth

(Attachment asked: retention matrix / SOC2 evidence)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Shah <rajiv.shah@olivehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying training guarantees + retention windows

Rajiv — thanks for the clear asks. Short version up front: Redwood does not use customer request or content to train, update, or fine-tune our public models by default for any customers on our platform (hosted or dedicated). For Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments customers control model artifacts entirely. Below I include a concise Q&A and the operational timeline for deletion. I attached our SOC2 summary and a proposed retention schedule tailored for OliveHealth.

Q: "Do you ever use customer text to improve models?"
A: No. We have a company-wide policy and engineering guards that prevent customer request bodies from being added to training corpora. There is an exception path which is strictly opt-in and handled under a separate data sharing agreement; that work is never performed without explicit contract-level consent and documented change control.

Q: "Does this apply to logs/telemetry (latency/error traces)?"
A: Operational telemetry used for platform health is generally aggregated and redacted by default. Error traces that include user content (rare) are retained only long enough to triage and are purged according to the schedule below unless you request an audit export.

Deletion/Retention timeline (typical hosted API flow):
- 0–24h: Deletion request acknowledged; we validate scope and owner.
- 24h–7d: Primary data and any live caches (including KV/prefix caches) are deleted.
- 7d–30d: Rolling backup windows — backups that may contain the data are scheduled for scrub or filtered deletion; most customers are fully removed from backups by day 30.
- 30d–90d: Ancillary logs and anonymized metrics used for systemic monitoring are kept (no PII/plaintext request bodies).

For Dedicated accounts we can shorten the backup scrub window via contractual SLA. For Private deployments, deletion is managed at the customer side unless you purchase Redwood-managed backups — in which case we follow your agreed retention contract.

I'll loop in Rishi and Monica for any deeper engineering notes.

Best,
Tessa
Account Exec — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

(Attachments: SOC2-2027-redwood.pdf, retention_schedule_olivehealth.xlsx)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Shah <rajiv.shah@redwoodhealth.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-15T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying training guarantees + retention windows

Rajiv — quick engineering clarification following Tessa's note:

- Model training/data pipelines are isolated from the inference request plane. There is a hard boundary: inference traffic does not flow into our model training buckets.

- Caching: we employ ephemeral KV caches to speed repeated prefixes. These caches are memory-resident and are flushed on deletion requests; they are not used as training inputs.

- Debugging snapshots: when a customer files a support ticket that requires reproducing an issue we may create a narrow snapshot that includes the request and minimal surrounding context. Those snapshots are labeled, access-controlled, and have a max retention window of 14 days unless waived by an escalation ticket.

- Backups: we use incremental backups. Conservative scrub means full removal can take up to the window Tessa outlined. If OliveHealth needs an accelerated deletion clause, we can define a contractual RPO for backups and add a dedicated runbook.

If you want, we can include a short appendix describing how to request a secure proof of deletion for a given data-id.

Thanks,
Rishi
Sr. Engineer, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Rajiv Shah <rajiv.shah@olivehealth.com>

Date: 2028-06-15T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying training guarantees + retention windows

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple follow-ups: 1) Can you confirm whether developer/admin logs (who called the API, token IDs) are retained beyond 30 days? We need at least 90-day audit trails for access logs per our policy. 2) For the opt-in training path, what is the exact legal control? Is there an SOW or an amendment we can see that binds the opt-in to explicit examples/data and revocation?

If you can provide a short export sample (redacted) showing how deletion is enacted, that'd be appreciated. We'll include the SOC2 and your notes in our assessment memo.

-Rajiv

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Shah <rajiv.shah@olivehealth.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-16T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying training guarantees + retention windows

Rajiv — short answers: 1) Access/audit logs: we retain authentication and access logs (token usage, IP, timestamp) 90 days by default for hosted customers; this is configurable for Dedicated/Private with enterprise packages. Content payloads are not stored in those auth logs. 2) Opt-in training: yes — it is governed by a written amendment (Data Use Addendum) and an SOW that defines scope, sample sets, revocation terms, and a rollback plan. Revocation triggers cessation of data transfer to training pipelines and a contractual requirement for Redwood to delete derivative artifacts where feasible; we include those clauses in our standard DUA template.

I'll attach a redacted export sample and the DUA excerpt to the HubSpot record and can set up a short call with legal if you'd like.

Next steps proposed:
- We drop the standard retention_schedule_olivehealth.xlsx into your assessment folder (done).
- If you need the accelerated backup scrub clause, we draft a short SLA amendment and share for your review.
- Offer: 1-month trial on Dedicated with the accelerated deletion clause baked in so you can validate deletion timelines operationally.

Let me know which you prefer and I can route to Contracts.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
